thread:
mira: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing we split the connector surface into two explicit contracts: a tiny bootstrap handshake and a separate steady-state dataplane contract. Goal: make onboarding lightweight for Private/VPC customers and reduce upgrade blast radius.

mira: Bootstrap = auth proof, minimal routing info (egress IPs / NAT mapping), cert thumbprint. Steady = session pinning, KV-sync, metrics stream, long-lived tunnels.

dan: sketch of minimal bootstrap fields? also, how do we avoid re-auth when we transition to steady-state?

mira: example:```
{
  "type":"bootstrap",
  "tenant_id":"T-123",
  "cert_proof":"sig:v1",
  "egress_ip":"10.2.3.4/32"
}
```

kevin: ok that helps. question: who rotates cert_proof? CP or connector? if CP rotates, connectors need a refresh flow w/ grace TTL. session-token TTL needs to be > handshake window or we get churn.

lea: TL;DR rollout: 1) implement bootstrap-only server side that accepts old connectors, 2) ship connector v2 that does bootstrap+opt-in steady, 3) canary steady to 5 tenants, 4) migrate by flipping a per-tenant flag. fallback path = proxying via regional relay.

kevin: also we must decide where TLS is terminated for steady: keep TLS end-to-end to connector (preferred for Private) vs terminate at regional relay (cheaper for Hosted). This affects cert lifecycle and mTLS model.

mira: agreed. proposal: bootstrap requires proof signed by tenant KMS/HSM or a short-lived token from CP. steady can upgrade with a second-step mutual-auth using the same cert thumbprint. That avoids double-auth prompt but ensures freshness.

dan: what about ip preservation + NAT hairpin for on-prem customers? bootstrap may need to include source-ip-hint and keepalive-port so steady can bind correctly.

lea: metrics we will track during rollout: handshake_fail_rate, steady_transition_latency_ms, steady_disconnects_per_hour, ip_mismatch_count. add alert if handshake_fail_rate > 0.5% during canary.

kevin: migration risk: connectors with older kernels that don't support kv-sync will hit a noop path. need feature-gate header in handshake to avoid timeouts. e.g., `X-Connector-Features: bootstrap,kv-sync-v1`

mira: good call. also add a compatibility-mode response field `transition_suggested:true|false` to let CP tell connector to stay in bootstrap-only for X minutes.

infra-bot: :gear: deploy-bot started canary rollout: connector-surface-split/v2 -> infra-canary-3 (logs: https://deploys.internal/redwood/3581237890) :eyes:

lea: ops checklist for canary — pre-create tenant flags, extra retention on handshake logs for 72h, and a manual rollback playbook if ip_leak_attempts > 0.

dan: small UX note: add clear error codes `BX_401_BOOTSTRAP_EXPIRED`, `BX_409_FEATURE_UNSUPPORTED` so we don't have to reverse-engineer logs.

mira: noted. next steps: I'll update the RFC doc with the handshake JSON example, add the feature-gate header, and write the rollout runbook. @kevin @lea can you review the runbook by EOD?

kevin: will review.

lea: on it.

infra-bot: canary metrics: handshake_success=98.9%, steady_upgrade_attempts=12 (0 failures so far) — will post 30m aggregate.
